[NLFC.5.2] A test's first act after creating an engine should be to take the
clock off live.

The engine starts in live mode ([NLFC.1.4]). The switch puts the monotonic
clock at 0 and leaves the wall clock unset ([NLFC.5.4]), and the test then
sets the timeline it wants explicitly ([NLFC.5.3]), so every time-driven effect
is under its control from the first input on.

Switching later is refused: once the engine has sampled its clock, which an
input does and a pump does with no input, the switch to mock returns
`DS_ERR_STATE` ([NLFC.5.4]). Anything time-driven that ran
before it would have run against wall time and would not reproduce
([NLFC.5.1]).
